heading: M3-Q30 (V2-D3.7), Select TWO
question:
A team integrates: (1) an internal API used by one
service, (2) a device capability that exists only as a CLI.

Which TWO are correct? Select TWO.

choices.A: Direct API for the single internal pair.
choices.B: CLI wrapper for the CLI-only device capability.
choices.C: MCP server for the single pair.
choices.D: MCP server for the one-off CLI.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "one service... exists only as a
CLI." Why: one pair takes the direct API. LI-only takes the wrapper.
C and D pay protocol tax for single uses. Counterfactual: none.

heading: M3-Q31 (V2-D3.8)
question:
A support agent uses 40 tools. The SLA is 15 seconds.
Token costs are the top complaint. Wrong-tool picks climb.

Which strategy fits?

choices.B:
Progressive discovery: names first, schemas on demand. The loose
SLA absorbs the round trip. Tokens and pick accuracy improve.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "40 tools... SLA is 15 seconds... Wrong-tool
picks climb." Why: large surface plus loose SLA is the discovery
win condition. Counterfactual: A wins with 6 tools and a 1-second SLA.

heading: M3-Q32 (V2-D4.1)
question:
A fraud detector's requirement is "catch fraud." The team
must set the acceptance threshold.

What is the correct threshold shape?

choices.B: Recall on confirmed fraud is at or above 95%. The false-positive rate is at or below 2%. Measure this on a held-out set.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "'catch fraud.'" Why: vague requirements
become measured thresholds with the metric, the line, and the
measurement set named. D measures memorization. Counterfactual: A wins
never as a threshold.

heading: M3-Q33 (V2-D4.1)
question:
A voice bot needs fast responses. The team sets the p95 acceptance threshold under 2 seconds. No one answers for the threshold.

Which link of the Lesson 7-4A requirement chain is still
missing?

choices.A: Nothing. The requirement, the metric, the threshold, and the owner are all present.
choices.B: The owner. No one answers for the threshold.
choices.C:
The requirement.
No one wrote "fast responses."
choices.D: The metric. No one named latency.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "No one is named to answer for the
threshold." Why: the Lesson 7-4A chain runs requirement, metric,
threshold, owner. The scenario gives the first three. Without a named
owner, the threshold drifts when the traffic mix changes. A is the
trap: "the team" is not a named owner. C and D contradict the stated
scenario. Counterfactual: A wins when a named role owns the threshold
and reviews it on a cadence.

heading: M3-Q34 (V2-D4.2)
question:
A team grades answers with a judge model. Human review of
100 sampled grades shows the judge is right 60% of the time.

What is the conclusion?

choices.B:
The judge is not calibrated. 60% agreement is near chance on graded scales. Do not trust its grades. Fix or replace the judge.
Or grade with code and humans.
choices.C: Sample more. Hope for a good result.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "right 60% of the time." Why: the grading
ladder requires calibrated judges. 60% agreement means the grades are
noise. Counterfactual: A wins at 95% agreement with the disagreements
characterized.

heading: M3-Q35 (V2-D4.2), Select TWO
question:
An eval set for a code assistant has only Python tasks.

Which TWO drawers are absent? Select TWO.

choices.A: Representative coverage of the other supported languages.
choices.B: Adversarial cases: prompts crafted to elicit insecure code.

explanation: The decisive phrase is "only Python tasks." The representative drawer misses all other languages. The adversarial drawer is empty. The threat (insecure code) has a name. Counterfactual: E wins as the malformed drawer, a third addition.

heading: M3-Q36 (V2-D4.3)
question:
A team runs an A/B test on a risky auto-refund change
with full traffic on day one.

What is wrong?

choices.B:
Risky changes go shadow first, then controlled exposure. Full
traffic on day one maximizes blast radius.
choices.C: A/B tests never apply to refunds.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "risky auto-refund change with full
traffic on day one." Why: V2-D4.3's shadow-first rule for risky
changes. The experiment design must bound user harm. Counterfactual: A
wins for a low-risk copy change.

heading: M3-Q37 (V2-D4.4)
question:
A vendor model update changed a support bot's tone. The tone became rude. Prompts, retrieval, and data are not changed.

Which layer failed?

choices.B:
The model version: vendor behavior changed under the same prompt.
Pin or change the version and re-run regression.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "after a vendor model update... unchanged."
Why: the change log names the version. Version behavior is a layer in
V2-D4.4. Fix it as a production change. Counterfactual: C wins when
the prompt changed.

heading: M3-Q38 (V2-D4.4), Select TWO
question:
A RAG bot hallucinates product specs. Traces show: chunks
arrive, but the top chunk is a forum post, not the spec sheet. The
spec sheet ranks fifth.

Which TWO fixes match the layer? Select TWO.

choices.A:
Boost authoritative sources in ranking (or filter to the spec
corpus).
choices.B: Add source-type metadata and prefer it at retrieval.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "top chunk is a forum post, not the
spec sheet." Why: the retrieval layer returns the wrong authority.
Ranking and metadata fixes belong to that layer. C and D fix proxies.
Counterfactual: C wins when the spec chunk is top-ranked and the
answer still errs.

heading: M3-Q39 (V2-D4.5)
question:
A nightly job re-embeds 1M documents. Only 2% change per
night.

Which optimization fits?

choices.B: Incremental embedding: embed only changed documents, reuse the rest.

explanation:
Decisive phrase: "Only 2% change per night." Why: call
elimination is the V2-D4.5 lever. Re-embedding 98% unchanged documents
is pure waste. Counterfactual: A wins when change detection costs more
than re-embedding.
